quests.title: A Very Festive Problem

dialogue.t: I'm sorry to trouble you during this festive time, Traveler, but we're a little in over our heads at the moment. The number of people requiring medicine from Bubu Pharmacy always peaks during the Lantern Rite period.

dialogue.sit: Why does that happen...

dialogue.t: During the Lantern Rite, everyone puts their work aside to spend time with their families. Of course, there will be all manner of banquets, with fine food and drink flowing all around...
Suddenly, everyone's got indigestion, or else they're coming down with some malady or other...
I'm always encouraging people to not eat too much, but during a food-driven festival like this, my advice tends to fall on deaf ears.
Just now, a few more customers contacted me, asking if I could bring them some medicine for indigestion and other stomach problems. But I can't simply stop manning the pharmacy...
Traveler, if it's alright with you, could you help me deliver some medicine?

dialogue.sit: Where are Baizhu and Qiqi?

dialogue.t: Qiqi went out to gather some herbs and still isn't back yet... It's highly possible that she might have gotten lost somewhere due to her poor memory again...
As for Dr. Baizhu, I think he's probably doing some medical research or something else of that nature. Either way, it's not my place to ask.

dialogue.sit: Isn't there anyone else who can help?

dialogue.t: Well... No one else at the pharmacy is free at the moment...
So I'm afraid it's all up to you for now, Traveler.

dialogue.sit: Got it.

dialogue.t: Thank you. Here's the medicine. Please get them to Guanhai and Zhihua as quickly as you can.
I wonder if we have enough herbs left...
Ugh, I must've eaten something that didn't agree with me...

dialogue.sit: Here's some medicine from Herbalist Gui...

dialogue.t: Oh, thank you. This is that stomach medicine I asked him for, isn't it? I think I might be getting indigestion... my stomach's feeling mighty terrible right now.
I was just strolling through the city streets, having a bite to eat here and there, and before I knew it, I'd overeaten ...

dialogue.sit: What did you eat...?

dialogue.t: Hmm, fried rice, raw fish, some fruit, lots and lots of shrimp... Ah yes, and some excellent wine!

dialogue.sit: Well, that explains it...
You shouldn't overindulge, even during a festival.

dialogue.t: Well, that's what medicine is for, isn't it? Think about it — what's the point of a festival if you can't eat whatever you like?
Thanks for bringing the medicine, either way. I should probably take this opportunity to rest as well.
Argh, I need to take a breather...
Ow, ow, ow... It hurts... Excuse me? D—Did you want something?

dialogue.sit: Here's some medicine from Herbalist Gui...

dialogue.t: Wow, thanks! Just what I ordered... Fast turnaround time, I must say.
Ahh, I feel better already. Must've caught a chill last night from the sea breeze, I'll wager...

dialogue.sit: No indigestion for you?

dialogue.t: Hah, indigestion? Me? I'll have you know that I have an iron stomach — why, I ate three grilled fish in one sitting for my last meal!
Even now, not one of my friends can match my prowess at eating and drinking.
Alright, enough about that. I'd better finish this medicine real quick — I've got a drinking session to get to.

dialogue.sit: Make sure to take care of yourself.
Don't wait until your health is ruined.

dialogue.t: Hahaha, oh, don't worry about me. I'm not some old fogey!
Still, thanks for the concern. I'll be careful.
Ahh, that's much better... Now, what should I eat later, I wonder?
Thanks for your help. Have all the medicines been delivered?

dialogue.sit: I don't think any of them learned their lesson...
You're likely to hear from them again soon...

dialogue.t: Well, there's not much we can do about that. Stomach problems won't go away unless you watch your lifestyle. The best we can do is treat the symptoms whenever they show up.
But I suppose that I can rest easy for now, at least...

dialogue.sit: So, what about Xiao Lanterns...

dialogue.t: Oh... We don't generally release lanterns. The whole point of Xiao Lanterns is to make a wish, right? Well... What sort of wish would Bubu Pharmacy even make?
Other businesses may wish for their business to thrive and boom, but a pharmacy is in the business of curing disease and saving lives... we can't exactly wish for more sick people, can we?

dialogue.sit: You've got a good heart, Gui.
You're an honest man.

dialogue.t: Heh... Well, on a more personal level, of course I'd love to join in. I mean, it is a festival...
But I haven't made much headway in constructing a Xiao Lantern. These last few days have been much too busy...
I can only steal a few moments during my breaks to work on it, and even then I'm sure the Lantern Rite will be over by the time I finish...

dialogue.sit: I can help.

dialogue.t: W—Will you really? Wow, thank you so much!
Hmm, how many more deliveries of medicine do we need to make...
Ah, it's you. Have you finished that Xiao Lantern?

dialogue.sit: Here it is.

dialogue.t: Thank you ever so much.
This lantern is both well-shaped and sturdy. Heh, my craftsmanship pales in comparison to yours...
In that case, we'll release this lantern later at night. I know a good spot.
In the meantime, I need to think of what I should wish for...
What should I wish for...
Ah, you're here. I've already written my wish on the lantern.
This is good timing... Let's release this lantern.
As for my wish... I ultimately wished for everyone in Liyue to be healthy and well.

dialogue.sit: And as for Bubu Pharmacy's business?

dialogue.t: Well, this was my personal wish, after all.
I put prescriptions together because I do not wish for people to be tormented by illness.
There's an old saying that sums this up nicely: "Dusty old medicine sat on the shelf, a small price to pay for a world of good health."
Not to mention that I'd be less busy if everyone remained healthy! That'd be a good thing, in my books...
...Oh no! I've suddenly remembered! There's still a customer I haven't delivered medicine to...
I'm sorry — I have to go! Happy Lantern Rite!
